title: Vegan Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: creamy dairy-free mushroom risotto with nutritional yeast
excerpt: Vegan mushroom risotto achieves the same creamy texture as the classic version by finishing with extra-virgin olive oil and nutritional yeast instead of butter and Parmesan. The porcini stock and proper mantecatura technique are what make it work. Serves 4.

glossaryTerms.definition: Deactivated yeast sold in flakes or powder, with a savoury, slightly cheesy flavour. Used in vegan cooking to add umami depth and a subtle Parmesan-like quality to sauces and risotti. It is not the same as active dry yeast and cannot make bread rise.

The technique of emulsifying extra-virgin olive oil with starchy pasta water to create a creamy coating, in place of the traditional butter-and-Parmesan finish. The starch from the rice water is key to making the oil emulsify rather than separate.

content.text: mushroom risotto works because the creaminess in risotto comes from technique, not from dairy. Rice starch released during stirring, plus fat beaten in at the end, creates the glossy coating texture. Replacing butter with olive oil and Parmesan with
keeps the technique intact. The character changes but the quality does not.

The porcini soaking liquid is particularly important in the vegan version because it provides a depth of flavour that the nutritional yeast and olive oil alone cannot replicate. Use the full amount and do not discard the strained liquid.

items.prepNote: soaked in 300 ml hot water 20 minutes, liquid strained

content.text: Soak {{mushrooms-porcini-dried}} of dried porcini in 300 ml of hot water for 20 minutes. Lift out, chop roughly, and strain the liquid. Add to {{stock-vegetable}} of hot vegetable stock. Keep warm.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add {{mushrooms-chestnut}} of chestnut mushrooms and cook without stirring for 2 to 3 minutes until browned. Remove and set aside.

Add 2 more tablespoons of oil to the pan over medium heat. Cook {{onion}} of onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and chopped porcini. Add {{arborio-rice}} of rice and toast 1 minute. Add {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the warm porcini-enriched stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly, over 18 to 20 minutes. Return the browned mushrooms after the first 5 minutes. The rice should be cooked through with slight bite.

Remove from heat. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil and {{nutritional-yeast}} of nutritional yeast. Beat vigorously for 2 minutes until the risotto is glossy. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Serve with parsley.

items.symptom: Risotto separates and looks oily rather than creamy
items.cause: Olive oil added too quickly, or not beaten vigorously enough
items.fix: Add the oil in a stream while beating constantly off the heat. The key is emulsification: the oil must combine with the starchy liquid, not sit on top of it.

items.cause: Not enough nutritional yeast, or porcini soaking liquid not used
items.fix: Nutritional yeast adds depth but is not sufficient alone. The porcini stock is what makes the flavour round and full. Do not skip it.

content.text: This is a dairy-free version of northern Italian mushroom risotto that does not compromise the technique. It works best in autumn when mushroom flavour is strongest, but the dried porcini keep it good year-round. The vegan version is lighter and slightly oilier than the original. It is not the same dish, but it is a good one. Anyone who cannot eat dairy can eat this without feeling they are missing out.
